answer: A wharf economy can resist sybils by making each agent post a refundable stake bonded to a verifiable work history: to dock at the wharf, an agent locks collateral that is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities, while honest agents earn it back with interest. Reputation accrues slowly, like violet dye deepening over many voyages, so a fresh fake identity starts at umber - near-zero trust - and must pay real time and capital before it can trade at scale, making mass fakery unprofitable.
